engine_rules.name: Restrict quartal voicing to 4ths, 5ths, 2nds, 7ths
engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal voicing containing a 3rd or 6th as primary structural interval
engine_rules.anchor: Primary intervals: 4ths and 5ths

engine_rules.name: Treat quartal and tertial harmony as structural opposites
engine_rules.falsifier: Quartal voicing treated as tertial chord with added color tones
engine_rules.anchor: tertial harmony and quartal harmony are pretty much exact opposites.

engine_rules.name: Avoid B-Eb in quartal voicings
engine_rules.falsifier: A B-Eb interval in quartal context that does not collapse to triadic sound
engine_rules.anchor: they don't work very well in a 4th voicings context.

engine_rules.name: Use drop-D pedal for quartal cycle exploration in D Dorian
engine_rules.falsifier: D Dorian containing an avoid note that obstructs free pedal exploration
engine_rules.anchor: tune the low E string down a whole step to D. Use the low D string as a pedal

engine_rules.name: Prefer D Dorian as avoid-note-free quartal context
engine_rules.falsifier: Another Dorian mode that also has zero avoid notes
engine_rules.anchor: there aren't any "avoid" notes in Dorian

engine_rules.name: Alternate arpeggio direction on successive chord positions
engine_rules.falsifier: Two successive chords arpeggiated in the same direction
engine_rules.anchor: Arpeggiate up the first chord, then down the second chord

engine_rules.name: Apply every voicing through all five M-Lode deployment modes
engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing family for which fewer than five deployment modes are applicable
engine_rules.anchor: 1. melodies 2. arpeggios 3. counterpoint (2 simultaneous voices) 4. 3-part chords 5. 4-part chords

engine_rules.name: Move each voice by 2nd, 3rd, or common tone across diatonic cycle positions
engine_rules.falsifier: A voice moving by a 4th or larger between adjacent cycle positions without common-tone annotation
engine_rules.anchor: All of the M-Lode is based on voice-leading.

engine_rules.name: Mark non-moving voices as c.t. in voice-leading analysis
engine_rules.falsifier: A static voice omitted from or merged with moving voices in the analysis grid

engine_rules.name: Analyze every voicing in paired Intervallic and Functional grids
engine_rules.falsifier: An analysis grid that omits either intervallic or functional dimension

engine_rules.name: Apply two distinct voice-leadings at Cycles 2 and 7
engine_rules.falsifier: Cycles 2 or 7 resolved with a single voice-leading without addressing the diatonic 5th voice-crossing
engine_rules.anchor: Cycles 2 and 7 have two different voice-leadings.

engine_rules.name: Derive new voicing variants by inserting an octave between any two voices
engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing expansion that adds a non-octave interval between voices
engine_rules.anchor: inserting an octave between any 2 voices within a 3-part chord or a 4-part chord

engine_rules.name: Apply octave insertion equally to 3-part quartal voicings
engine_rules.falsifier: Octave insertion applied only to tertial chord families and not quartal
engine_rules.anchor: Of course, all of this applies to the 3-part 4th voicings as well

engine_rules.name: Select drop voicing type from canonical set
engine_rules.falsifier: A drop voicing type not derivable from the canonical close-voicing octave-insertion process
engine_rules.anchor: Drop 4 is an option.

engine_rules.name: Restrict Drop 3 and 4, Double Drop 2/Drop 4 to fingerstyle players
engine_rules.falsifier: Drop 3 and 4 executed comfortably with a pick
engine_rules.anchor: only for finger-style guitarists] would be: Drop 3 and 4

engine_rules.name: Derive 3-part subset from any 4-part chord by dropping one voice
engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than four valid omission configurations for a 4-part diatonic chord
engine_rules.anchor: it just amounts to leaving out one of the voices... There are 4 possible configurations.

engine_rules.name: Fill any voice motion of a 3rd with a diatonic passing tone
engine_rules.falsifier: A voice motion by 3rd that cannot accommodate a diatonic passing tone
engine_rules.anchor: Anytime one of the voices moves a distance of a 3rd, you can fill in that interval with a melodic passing tone.

engine_rules.name: Apply passing tones to both voices when two voices simultaneously move in 3rds
engine_rules.falsifier: Two voices moving in simultaneous 3rds where only one receives a passing tone
engine_rules.anchor: two voices move in 3rds

engine_rules.name: Begin voicing and arpeggio practice at 4-way close density
engine_rules.falsifier: Beginning M-Lode arpeggio practice with open or drop voicings before 4-way close
engine_rules.anchor: look at all of the 4-way close options within the M-Lode

engine_rules.name: Seek open-string-playable versions of 4-way close voicings
engine_rules.falsifier: A 4-way close voicing position where no open-string variant exists on guitar
engine_rules.anchor: find as many playable voicings for 4-way close as we can

engine_rules.name: Prefer C Harmonic Minor as scale context for M-Lode voicing exploration
engine_rules.falsifier: C Major or C Melodic Minor producing equal or richer chromatic voice-leading density than C Harmonic Minor
engine_rules.anchor: IT JUST SOUNDS BETTER IN HARMONIC MINOR

engine_rules.name: Treat C Harmonic Minor as highest chromatic density voice-leading environment
engine_rules.falsifier: C Major producing denser chromatic voice-leading than C Harmonic Minor
engine_rules.anchor: ending in C Harmonic Minor, which the method identifies as the most sonically rewarding and the most chromatically dense voice-leading environment in the entire system

engine_rules.name: Generate all 24 arpeggio orderings for any 4-part voicing
engine_rules.falsifier: A 4-part voicing with fewer than 24 distinct arpeggio orderings
engine_rules.anchor: Any [and ALL] 4-part voicings can be arpeggiated in 24 different sequences

engine_rules.name: Practice all 6 two-voice subsets of every 4-part chord
engine_rules.falsifier: A 4-part chord yielding more or fewer than 6 two-voice combinations
engine_rules.anchor: Play all 6 possible combinations of 2 voices

engine_rules.name: Practice all 4 three-voice subsets of every 4-part chord
engine_rules.falsifier: A 4-part chord yielding more or fewer than 4 three-voice combinations
engine_rules.anchor: Play all 4 possible combinations of 3 voices

engine_rules.name: Divide 4-part chord into two alternating 2-note call-and-response pairs
engine_rules.falsifier: A 4-part chord that cannot be divided into two meaningful 2-note groupings
engine_rules.anchor: divide the 4-part chord into two 2-note groupings

engine_rules.name: Approach spread cluster voicings with physical preparation
engine_rules.falsifier: A spread cluster voicing that is physically undemanding on guitar
engine_rules.anchor: BE VERY CAREFUL!!!

engine_rules.name: Treat voicings as unnamed harmonic objects for functional flexibility
engine_rules.falsifier: A system that names chord qualities to restrict voicing function to one harmonic role
engine_rules.anchor: chords are deliberately left unnamed to preserve their harmonic flexibility across functions

engine_rules.name: Traverse every voicing family through all six diatonic cycles
engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing family traversed through fewer than six diatonic cycles
engine_rules.anchor: voice-led through six cycles in each of the three scales

engine_rules.name: Realize every voicing family in all three diatonic scale contexts
engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing family realized in only one or two of the three scale systems
engine_rules.anchor: every 3-part and 4-part chord voicing available within the three diatonic scales - C Major, C Melodic Minor, and C Harmonic Minor

engine_rules.name: Use the five 4-part families as the complete diatonic 4-part taxonomy
engine_rules.falsifier: A 4-part chord type within a seven-note diatonic scale not covered by these five families
engine_rules.anchor: these five 4-part chord families are not merely a selection but the only 4-part families possible within seven-note diatonic scales

engine_rules.name: Target 1000+ total voicings across the complete M-Lode system
engine_rules.falsifier: A complete M-Lode realization producing fewer than 1000 total voicings
engine_rules.anchor: 20 different 3-part chords (240 voicings), 30+ different 4-part chords (800+ voicings), and 1,000+ total voicings

engine_rules.name: Include 3-part Spread Clusters, 7th-no-5th, and 7th-no-3rd as M-Lode supplement families
engine_rules.falsifier: A 3-part omission-derived family outside these three types
engine_rules.anchor: three additional 3-part chord families within the M-Lode: 3-part Spread Clusters, 7th Chord (no 5th), and 7th Chord (no 3rd)

engine_rules.name: Enforce exact interval count for 3-part quartal voicing
engine_rules.falsifier: A 3-part quartal voicing with interval counts deviating from Two 2nds, Four 4ths, Two 5ths, One 7th
engine_rules.anchor: Two 2nds, Four 4ths, Two 5ths, One 7th

engine_rules.name: Apply MSRP memorized note-sequence drill at 3-part 4ths level
engine_rules.falsifier: M.S.R.P. drill applied before the 3-part 4ths entry level
engine_rules.anchor: The M.S.R.P. (memorized note-sequence) drill loop appears at the 3-part 4ths level

engine_rules.name: Use index card strips for tactile voice isolation and reduction practice
engine_rules.falsifier: An alternative practice aid that achieves equivalent voice isolation without physical notation strips
engine_rules.anchor: eight half-inch strips cut from a 4x6 card

engine_rules.name: Generate melodies by arpeggiation of quartal voicing shapes
engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal arpeggiation that produces no usable melodic material
engine_rules.anchor: arpeggiate quartal voicings to discover melodies

engine_rules.name: Expect three common tones and one voice moving by 4th in Cycle 7 Drop 2
engine_rules.falsifier: Cycle 7 Drop 2 position with fewer than three common tones between adjacent chords

engine_rules.name: Ground every M-Lode voicing decision in voice-leading, not chord quality
engine_rules.falsifier: An M-Lode voicing chosen by chord quality or function rather than voice-leading economy
engine_rules.anchor: All of the M-Lode is based on voice-leading.
